answer: Each identity claims one knoll post and locks a 70-credit bond to a ferrous badge keyed to it. At dawn the holder taps the badge at the reader, logging serial, post, and minute. An auditor recomputes attendance from the post log; a missing, late, or duplicate tap burns the bond. First muster fee 34; kth fake 34+5(k-1), so 1,000 fakes pay 2,531,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-muster ring fails: one stand-in cannot reach distant posts in one dawn window, and a twice-tapped badge burns both claims. An honest agent pays 34 once and recovers the bond after a clean audit.
